amendments.rule: Read `בֵּין X וּבֵין Y` by the connective the ASV actually writes. Where it is recast as *X from Y*, the second `בֵּין` carries *from*, while the first `בֵּין` and its waw are `unrepresented`. Where the ASV preserves *between X and Y*, the first `בֵּין` takes *between*, the waw takes *and*, and the repeated second `בֵּין` is `unrepresented`. Do not transfer the *and* to the repeated preposition: the waw is the morpheme that licenses it. **Hebrew also writes the second member with `לְ` in place of a repeated `בֵּין`, and the same reading follows the morpheme that is actually there.** In `בֵּין X לְ Y` → *between X and Y* the `בֵּין` takes *between* and the `לְ` takes the *and*, exactly as the waw does above, because the `לְ` is what stands where the connective stands and no waw is present to claim it: `בֵּין שֶׂה לָשֶׂה` → *between sheep and sheep* is the shape. Do not mark such a `לְ` `unrepresented` in order to leave the *and* `added`, and do not reach for rule 14's last sentence: that sentence governs a connective no morpheme answers to, and here one does. **Where the phrase runs on into further `לְ` members the ASV writes as bare coordinated nouns, only the `לְ` standing where the ASV writes its connective takes one.** `בֵּין שֶׂה לָשֶׂה לָאֵילִים וְלָעַתּוּדִים` → *between sheep and sheep, the rams and the he goats* gives *and* to the first `לְ`, leaves the two later ones `unrepresented` under rule 40, and gives the second written *and* to the waw. Count the phrase's connective morphemes against the ASV's connectives and read which pair of members each stands between, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s.
amendments.why: The chapter twice met `בֵּין X לְ Y`, which rule 26 as written does not reach: it legislates only for the repeated `בֵּין` with its waw, and its closing sentence — that the waw is the morpheme that licenses the *and* — reads, out of context, as a reason to deny the *and* to any other morpheme, which would leave EZK.34.17 and EZK.34.22 with an `added` connective standing beside a `לְ` that has nothing. The amendment states the case rule 26 had not considered rather than adding a rule that points back at it. Evidence: EZK.34.17 and EZK.34.22 both give the *and* to the `לְ`, independently and consistently; the corpus aligns `לְ` to *and* in 19 units, so nothing there is contradicted; and rule 26's own principle, read by the connective the ASV actually writes and give it to the morpheme that stands in its place, is what carries the extension. The final sentence records EZK.34.17's longer list, where the ASV drops the preposition for the remaining members and rule 40 disposes of them, so that the count does not silently promote a second `לְ` to carry the waw's *and*.

conventions: רעה with a bare מִרְעֶה: where the ASV reaches the verb's complement through a supplied preposition, that preposition belongs to the verb's unit under rule 44 and not to the noun under rule 33, because מִרְעֶה after רעה is the verb's own complement rather than an adverbial accusative. Applied at 34.14 (on fat pasture shall they feed) and 34.18 (to have fed upon the good pasture); the same reading gives of to the verb in 34.18's to have drunk of the clear waters and in 34.15's will be the shepherd of my sheep. Where a Hebrew preposition or an object marker is present it takes the word instead, as ב does at 34.14 and 34.18 and אֶל at 34.13 and 34.14.

בֵּין X לְ Y (34.17, 34.22): the לְ of the second member takes the ASV's and, on rule 26's reasoning that the morpheme standing where the connective stands is what licenses it; the בֵּין keeps between and nothing is added. Where the phrase runs on into further לְ members that the ASV writes as bare coordinated nouns (34.17 לָאֵילִים, לָעַתּוּדִים), those לְ are unrepresented under rule 40 and the waw takes the and written for it.

מִבְּלִי רֹעֶה (34.5) is read exactly as מֵאֵין רֹעֶה (34.8): the privative מִן takes the complementizing because and בְּלִי takes the negation together with its presentative frame, there was no, headed on the negation. Rule 48's last clause names אַיִן by lemma, but בְּלִי is likewise a present negative morpheme and takes its English before a supplied reading does; the pair splits rather than fusing because the ASV has spent words on both, so rule 30's מֵאֵין -> without condition is unmet.

The אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה formula (34.2, 34.8, 34.10, 34.11, 34.15, 34.17, 34.20, 34.30, 34.31 and the נְאֻם variants): אֲדֹנָי takes the supplied the Lord under rule 15, its 1cs suffix is unrepresented because the ASV writes no possessive answering to it, and יְהוִה takes Jehovah. BSB represents that suffix in all nine places; the difference is conventional and is not a review candidate.

An appositional even. Where the ASV writes even before a phrase whose every morpheme already holds its own English and no object marker stands on it, the word is added under rule 16's limit: 34.2's say unto them, even to the shepherds leaves it added, the appositive's own לְ having taken to. Where even instead stands on an emphatic pronoun doubling one already rendered, it is what English spends on that pronoun and joins its unit headed on the pronoun: הִנְנִי אָנִי -> Behold, I, even I at 34.11 and 34.20 gives even I to אָנִי. The subtraction test rules 16 and 31 use is what separates them, since dropping the word at 34.2 diminishes no morpheme's rendering while dropping it at 34.11 and 34.20 removes the whole contribution of a pronoun whose only work is emphasis. Competing reading: mark those two added as well, on the ground that I alone already realizes אָנִי.

report: One genuine cross-verse split, in EZK.34.14. A preposition the ASV supplies to reach a bare Hebrew complement of רעה is kept with the verb at 34.18 (הַמִּרְעֶה הַטּוֹב תִּרְעוּ -> to have fed upon; מִשְׁקַע מַיִם תִּשְׁתּוּ -> to have drunk of) and at 34.15 (אֶרְעֶה צֹאנִי -> will be the shepherd of), but given to the noun under rule 33 at 34.14 (וּמִרְעֶה שָׁמֵן תִּרְעֶינָה -> on fat pasture). Rule 44's limit decides it: a word supplied for a direct object is licensed by the English verb's valency, one supplied for an adverbial accusative by the noun's own case-function, and מִרְעֶה after רעה is the verb's complement in both verses. Patched 34.14 only; 34.15 and 34.18 already read correctly.

The candidate table's מִרְעֶה Ncmsa->Aamsa bucket (pasture vs on pasture) is the mechanical trace of that split. Every other multi-treatment bucket read out is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different contexts. אֵת takes with, for, over or even only where the marker stands on the phrase that word introduces (34.3, 34.4, 34.8, 34.11, 34.23) and is unrepresented where the ASV writes the object bare (34.2, 34.7, 34.8, 34.10, 34.12, 34.14, 34.16, 34.18, 34.21, 34.23, 34.26, 34.27). The resultative לְ is unrepresented throughout (34.5, 34.8 twice, 34.10, 34.22, 34.23, 34.24) and takes an English word only where the ASV writes one (34.10 for, 34.25 with, 34.29 unto and for). מִן is read off the ASV at 34.5, 34.10, 34.12, 34.13, 34.25 and 34.27.

The interrogative particle is not a split. At 34.2 הֲלוֹא -> should is a fronted auxiliary and takes the particle under rule 17's first clause; at 34.18 הַמְעַט -> Seemeth it is an inverted lexical linking verb with no auxiliary written, so rule 17's inversion clause leaves the particle unrepresented and rule 20 hands the copula with its dummy to the predicate מְעַט. Rule 17 draws that line itself, and both units name the competing reading.

The appositional even at 34.2 (added, no marker standing on לָרֹעִים, whose own לְ already holds to) and the emphatic even at 34.11 and 34.20 (aligned to אָנִי) are two constructions, not one analysed twice: the subtraction test rules 16 and 31 use finds that dropping the word at 34.2 diminishes no morpheme's rendering, while dropping it at 34.11 and 34.20 takes away the whole contribution of a pleonastic pronoun whose only work is emphasis. Recorded as a convention with the competing reading named, since a later reader would otherwise re-litigate it.

BSB: none of the 45 disagreements is an error. The four recurring classes (R x13, Sp1cs x9 on אֲדֹנָי, To x10, Rd x4) are the documented convention difference, BSB attaching the preposition to its phrase and rendering the divine-title suffix. The singletons are contract-mandated: 34.6 the repeated אֵין (rule 22), 34.9 the vocative article (rule 36), 34.12 and 34.18 articles the ASV writes no the for (rules 29, 47), 34.11 and 34.20 waws the ASV leaves unrendered (rule 14), 34.18 the paragogic nun (rule 32), 34.31 the resumptive אַתֶּם (rule 22). Nothing was changed to improve the rate.

Also verified as internally uniform and left alone: the אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה formula in ten verses; לָכֵן fused at 34.7, 34.9, 34.20; לָבֶטַח at 34.25, 34.27, 34.28; בְּתוֹךְ at 34.12 and 34.24; the construct-plus-article pattern of חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה and its kin at 34.5, 34.8, 34.13, 34.27, 34.28, 34.29; the four waw-plus-negative neither fusions at 34.4 and the three at 34.8, 34.10, 34.28, 34.29; and the two as for units marked added at 34.17 and 34.19 under rule 16's third-family limit.
